subject.title: [Bug/Docs]: local+hybrid memory_search quality can appear unstable due to extraPaths path drift + benchmark-file contamination

question: Should OpenClaw add a public memorySearch exclusion contract now, and should that contract cover builtin indexing only or also QMD, status diagnostics, and docs?
rationale: The remaining work would add public config and alter which files enter the recall corpus, while repository policy treats memory/session-state and config/default surfaces as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
options.body: Repair and land the open `excludePaths` PR with explicit builtin-only scope, index-identity coverage, and docs while tracking QMD and diagnostic parity separately.

options.title: Require cross-backend contract
options.body: Pause the exclusion work until builtin indexing, QMD, watcher behavior, docs, and status diagnostics share one path-hygiene model.

options.title: Docs and diagnostics only
options.body: Defer public exclusion config and improve memory status/docs guidance around path drift, broad `extraPaths`, and benchmark contamination.

recommendation.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
recommendation.body: Repair and land the open `excludePaths` PR with explicit builtin-only scope, index-identity coverage, and docs while tracking QMD and diagnostic parity separately.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses memory indexing, config compatibility, and docs, where steipete has the strongest recent history in the affected files.
